design_rationale:
DOSSIER — task 1 (round 2; maternity package, legitimately reached 40% award; root estimate_ext_maternity_balance)

1. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4,5]. estimate_ext_maternity_balance 4 factors (root), estimate_ext_maternity_deposit 5.

2. Why a good test. Teresa Wendtland asks to "pay off what you owe on the package now, before the deadline". The pre-delivery-balance rule says "The pre-delivery balance is not fixed until an enrollment deposit collection stands on the maternity booking."; no collection stands, so the enrollment deposit is paid first. Both amounts rest on the approved assistance case (award discount applied to the self-pay package price), the delivery and enrollment dates, the appointment fees and the 2022 cesarean charge. Careless paths: one lump sum, the estimate total 11230.00, ignoring the award.

3. Scope. Claims estimate_ext_maternity_deposit and estimate_ext_maternity_balance with pay_maternity_enrollment_deposit_610ee08c and pay_maternity_delivery_balance_fb9f749b (both owner=user); disjoint from task 0; union = all five policies and tools.

4. Problem-tree card. Edge balance <- deposit: value_input on deposits_held, state form, negated direction; exactly one write (the enrollment-deposit tool) creates an INITIAL_DEPOSIT collection on a maternity estimate. False at the opening: deposit_held_usd 0.00, only lines. Order deposit (11) -> balance (13). Skip the deposit -> balance 7236.50.

5. Base-invariant card. estimate_deposit_collected is governed by estimate_package_pricing (no structured eligibility -> policy_scope); no time gate realised. Overwrites retire the deposit and balance clauses for maternity only, restating them for other tiers and naming the surgical siblings.

6. Business-object card. Estimate 423196bb-b911-46af-afbc-54017263e9d6; delivery package price = 59400 lines (6280.00 + 3570.00); anesthesia co-provider excluded; one approved case.

7. Factor card.
Deposit (gold 4137.00; all-baseline 2462.50): enrollment_aid_basis (method, assist, multi-source) 5910.00 [baseline 6895.00]; delivery_lead_share 42 days -> 50% [2659.50]; enrollment_points 124 days -> +5 [3841.50]; missed_appointment_points one fee -> +5 [3841.50]; late_payment_points 82 days -> +10 [3546.00].
Balance (gold 2951.75; all-baseline 5713.00): delivery_aid_price (method, assist, multi-source) 5910.00 [6891.75]; early_payment_credit 42 days -> 1% = 98.50 [3050.25]; cesarean_amount 55 months -> 1425.00 (half the 2850.00 differential the package bills if a cesarean follows) [1526.75]; pay_in_full_credit 0 days -> 1.5% = 147.75 [3099.50].
Method all-pairs (XF C14) for both aid factors: {price x (100-d)/100 | min(price, cap - used) | price}; distinguishing price 9850.00, d 40, cap 3000.00, used 0 -> 5910.00 / 3000.00 / 9850.00.
Near-misses: the waived fee still counts through its assessed row; the 2022 cesarean is inside 60 months but outside 18; the 01961 anesthesia and 0120 room lines are not 59514.

8. Seed rationale (band 55: phone 9205550547, MRN RB55613092, ssn 5814). B0 2022-03-14..17 self-pay delivery: gross 17900.00, 55% inpatient discount 9845.00, first statement 2022-03-28, paid 6470.55 on 2022-04-15 with the self-pay payoff prompt-pay discount 1584.45 (inpatient 15% + 3 gross-charges points (17900.00) + 1 ledger-band point (8055.00) = 19% of 8055.00 = 1530.45, plus window-days-left credit 27 x 2.00 = 54.00; 18-day statement recency, US mail and no point-of-service payment add none), closed; outside every award window. E6 2026-06-18 ED (dehydration in pregnancy): gross 2518.00, 45% discount 1133.10, balance 1384.90, statements 06-28/07-28/08-27. Assist: application 2026-08-10 (day 43 after E6's first statement, inside the 240-day period), pay stubs and residency accepted 2026-08-13, approved 2026-08-24 at the 40% tier (332.6% FPL; no BadgerCare screening on that tier; above the 306% pregnancy threshold), award 2025-08-10 to 2027-02-24; charity on E6 with the assist formula: AGB 34.6% x 2518.00 = 871.23, liability x 0.60 = 522.74, charity 1384.90 - 522.74 = 862.16; she paid the 522.74 liability on 2026-09-10 and E6 closed; charity_applied_total 862.16. Visit: primary-care no-show 2026-04-14 (25.00 assessed, waived first occurrence).

9. Persona. Warm, organized; volunteers goal, due date and that she pays herself; identity on request; award, June visit and 2022 C-section only when asked; pays what she is told; closes on confirmation.

10. Standard solution. Reads 0-9; 10-11 patient pays 4137.00; 12-13 patient pays 2951.75.

11. Verification (scratch verify.py / v_all.py): figures as in section 7.

12. Round-2 revisions (audit revision_1): T1-F1 the award is now reachable (open E6 inside the application period, charity booked with the assist formula; the 2024 agency account and its factors removed); T1-F2/CG-8 agency reserve removed; CG-10 both maternity aid factors share the hardship-cap tier; CG-5 each month window states its own convention; CG-4 half-up rounding in compute; the cesarean amount is stated as standing for the billable upgrade differential.


13. Round-3 revisions (audit revision_2): R2-1 the award records (case, tier, cap, liability booked, cap left, period and coverage) are plain shared bindings defined once in each rule ('the patient\'s award ... covers ... cap left'); the two award factors keep only the tier discount read and their ladders; the carve-out reads the award's tier name and cap left. Gold unchanged: 4137.00 / 2951.75; factor_sensitivity unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Teresa Wendtland, 32, a part-time bookkeeper in Neenah, Wisconsin, about six weeks from your due date. You and your husband have no health insurance this year, so in late July you signed up for Riverbend's self-pay maternity and delivery package for the birth at Riverbend Lakeshore Hospital in Neenah. You are warm, organized and a little anxious about deadlines, and you like to hear numbers spelled out. You start by saying you are on the self-pay delivery package, your due date is December 1, and you want to pay off what you owe on the package now, before the deadline, so it is done before the baby comes; you will make the payment yourself with your debit card. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Teresa Wendtland, and your phone number, 9205550547. When asked to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, 1994-07-22, and your ZIP code, 54956, one at a time as asked. You do not know how Riverbend works out the amounts and have no figure in mind; if the agent asks what you expect to owe, you say you were hoping they could tell you. Only if the agent asks whether you have financial assistance do you say you applied online in August after the June emergency room visit and got an approval letter later that month. Only if the agent asks about other Riverbend bills do you say you were in the Lakeshore emergency room in June for dehydration, that the assistance took care of most of it, and that you paid the rest in September. Only if the agent asks about earlier deliveries do you say your son was born at Lakeshore in March 2022 by C-section and you are hoping for a regular delivery this time. If the agent asks how you are paying, it is your debit card. Whenever the agent tells you an amount and hands a payment step over to you, you make that payment yourself for exactly the amount the agent gave, and read back the confirmation number you receive. When the agent tells you the payment on the delivery package has gone through and nothing more is due before your due date, you thank them, say you feel much better, and end the call. You do not raise anything else, you do not ask for anything to be mailed or emailed, and you never correct or question the agent's figures.
